text: Such a big fan of Bodega Negra! I came here with four girls on a Saturday night for dinner and it was perfect. This place has a really good vibe and is perfect for dinner/drinks before a night out. The service here is also great - our server Lawrence was fun, nice and attentive. We each had one app, tacos and one drink and we got out of here for less than $50 per person. I had the Skirt Steak tacos, the Grilled Corn Salad and tried the Yuca Fries and the Sweet Plantains (plain without the cheese or crema) and everything was so good! I also asked for a custom tequila drink which was awesome. I would definitely recommend Bodegra Negra for a good group dinner that won't break the bank.

Title: Hit and Miss at Local Eatery

As someone who works in the area, I've frequented this spot for their enticing happy hour, featuring half-priced appetizers and drink specials from 4-7pm on weekdays. The wings have always been a highlight for me; they're particularly delicious. However, my latest visit for takeout lunch left something to be desired. Upon entering the eerily empty establishment, I found myself without a greeting or immediate assistance. It was only at the bar where I found service, which was, regrettably, less than welcoming.

Despite the lackluster interaction, I ordered the honey BBQ wings, which lived up to my memories – they were generously sized and quite scrumptious, accompanied by the classic celery and carrot sides. Service, on the contrary, could use some serious attention, especially given the absence of other patrons during my visit.

I'll likely return for their happy hour offerings but will give their takeout service a pass in the future.

I recently dined at this gem of a Japanese restaurant which boasted a serene atmosphere paired with impeccable service. Their culinary prowess shined through a diverse menu, especially with their high-quality Japanese offerings. I was particularly impressed by their extensive sake selection, which provides an excellent opportunity for pairing and exploration.

Every quarter they refresh their menu with a special feature, a thoughtful touch that keeps the dining experience fresh and enticing. The highlight of my visit was the unique sake affogato—a delightful blend of homemade milk ice cream, coconut jelly, fruits, and beans. This dessert struck the perfect balance between sweetness and portion size.

The standout savory dish was the Japanese eel, cooked to perfection, and served atop a bed of wonderfully flavored rice. Both dishes left a lasting impression, and I eagerly anticipate my next visit to see what new experiences await on their ever-evolving menu.

Title: A NYC Gem for Theatergoers

If you find yourself ravenous between theater shows and want both delicious and budget-friendly eats, this spot is a must-visit. For a mere $6-7, you can indulge in two scrumptious tacos, which is an absolute bargain in NYC. The salads, according to my friend's enthusiastic review, are equally delectable and well-priced at around $11. 

I personally savored the carne asada and chicken tacos, each packing a delightful spicy punch without overwhelming the palate. Additionally, the Brussels sprouts taco caught my eye and is on my list for next time. And for a humorous touch, check out their bathroom sign that playfully prohibits Instagramming mid-business. A quirky reminder that good food and good fun go hand in hand at this charming eatery.

Title: A Sweet Symphony at Dessert Haven

Dessert aficionados, take note! When they say "Dessert first," this charming spot takes it to heart. Every visit is a delightful surprise, thanks to their ever-changing seasonal offerings that keep your taste buds on their toes. Yet, amidst the novelty, the iconic 'plant' dessert remains a steadfast crown jewel.

What truly sets this eatery apart is the craftiness of its sweets, cookies, and the must-try bubble tea served in an eye-catching bulb. The menu is best enjoyed tapas-style—gather a group of friends to embark on a culinary expedition, allowing you to sample the spectrum of sumptuous desserts on offer.

In a nutshell, this dessert hub is the go-to for anyone looking to indulge in artfully crafted confections. Go ahead, give in to your sweet tooth—you won't be disappointed!

I had my doubts. Dig Inn (*ahem*, excuse me, it's much more sophisticatedly-named "Dig", now) hires a legitimate chef and suddenly expands its brand to include fine dining? I wasn't convinced. Sure, Dig Inn was my first favorite Chipotle-style, healthy, fast-casual eatery, but I didn't intuitively expect it to master the sit-down experience. Upon further reflection, it makes sense. Farm-to-table is at peak popularity and Dig Inn has supported that movement from the beginning. My sense, at this point, is that Dig smartly tagged a young, ambitious chef (Suzanne Cups) with vision that aligned with the company's values, ultimately let her do her thing, just with the "Dig" seal of approval on it. And while there are a few small kinks to work out, 232 Bleecker is doing a lot right. While the name of the restaurant is lazy, the menu is anything but. Veggie-centric with seasonal ingredients and plates great for sharing, the menu is wide-ranging and varied, making great use of all that soil has to offer. The service was just plain bad, to be blunt, but thankfully, that's an easy fix. The vision and concept of 232 Bleecker are outstanding, and that's what counts. Came here with a friend at 8:15 on Saturday. When booking my reservation, the interface enabled me to note whether I'd like chef's counter if available. I never decline a chance at getting a front row seat, so I wrote a little note saying I'd be delightful, if the setup was possible. We walked in, and luck was on our side -- chef's counter it was. 232 Bleecker -- and the name will never let us forget it -- is on a very hot corner. The previous occupant left because I'm sure the rent here is obscene. But this spot will do well -- surrounded by other health-conscious eateries (Bluestone Lane, Jack's Wife Freda, etc.), this is an area with great demand for this type of food. Quick initial plot twist with the alcohol situation here. We were indecisive when it came to drinks, because we hadn't known there was no liquor on the menu before arriving here. Wine/beer/cider only. This means that while there is a cocktail spread, all are made with ingredients likely unfamiliar to many. I've only had a handful of wine-based drinks in my lifetime, and I was never all that thrilled with them. At 232 Bleecker, however, they make it work in really impressive fashion. My friend got the Small Buck (amaro, sweet & dry vermouth, lemon, ginger), which tasted just like a well-executed spicy and rich whiskey drink, minus the whiskey. I ordered the 232 Spritz -(cocchi americano, westbrook gose -- made with cider instead of beer), which was fruity and refreshing. Both good drinks and the low ABV meant we could prance along into the wine section easily. Wine is the specialty here, though there's not a huge amount of variety in what you can order by the glass -- at least in the white wine section. All offerings are dry and crisp except one "bold and oaky" chardonnay which is the opposite of my cup of...wine. So we sampled a few other whites, all of which paired nicely with the food. I would like to pause here to say I think I would have enjoyed the drinks more had they not taken so long to come. Is it really that onerous to pour up two glasses and bring them over? We wanted to enjoy our wine with our food, but the constant delays with all of our drinks messed up the tempo and coordination, which was a shame. Our waitress was also generally not too helpful in our decision-making process and didn't seem to value efficiency. But as I said at the onset, this is an easier fix than a flawed menu.So lets get to that food. It was all fantastic. Vegetable-focused, fresh and seasonal ingredients, thoughtful preparations and great flavors. You can get more than enough variety and demonstration of technique ordering from the menu's large veg section alone. Plenty of good proteins for meat-eaters, but those dishes all feature delightful veggies of the rainbow as well. I wish we could've ordered it all, but we did our best. Eats, below:Smoked cod, nori aioli: A-Served with crackers, which are a must. Need that textural variety otherwise this falls a little flat. Still solid, just not as bold or impressive as the other dishes, could have used more nori. Also quite a lot of fish for a "snack".Beef tartare, broccoli leave: ARich, yummy, super flavorful and beautifully presented. Served with rice crackers if you want some crunch, but they're not absolutely imperative.Beets, black lentil, fried shallot: A+Sweet, crunchy, rich, salty, everything right going on here. Well-balanced, delicate and still powerful.Brussels sprouts, apple butter, spiced pecan: ARich and warming, far more elevated than any Brussels you'll find at Dig. A perfect winter dish with delightful accompaniments.Charred cauliflower, concord grape, sunflower butter: A+Others have said it, I'll repeat it: this is the star. This is as decadent as vegetables come. Earthy, nutty, sweet. And that char is perfection.

From the moment I stepped into this delightful eatery, I was whisked away on a nostalgic journey back to Spain – both in ambiance and taste. Each tapas dish served was a small treasure trove of explosive flavors, exactly as they should be but so often aren't in the bustling New York City food scene. Paired with a crisp glass of cava or a robust red wine, the dining experience was nothing short of sublime. It's been a long time since I've been graced with such authentic and joy-inducing Spanish cuisine. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

During a recent lunch outing with coworkers at this particular restaurant, we discovered a delightful prix-fixe menu. I savored every bite of the well-seasoned meatballs starter and succulent salmon main course. Moreover, my colleague's choice of the stuffed red peppers was both delicious and satisfying. Unfortunately, another coworker's chicken souvlaki fell short, being somewhat dry and lacking in flavor.

A highlight of our meal was the complimentary bread and pita basket, served with a delectable olive oil dip, which we enjoyed enough to ask for seconds. From previous visits, I can attest that their a la carte dips are nothing short of excellent. This place has its ups and downs, but it's absolutely worth checking out for a meal.

I had plans to go to Chick shop today for lunch until I found the place closed online. All the searches (google, yelp) of hummus/falafel places near Grand Central/Times Square led us straight into this place and that's how I decided to try their lunch. I was having a late lunch and it was off time (around 3PM) and I think apart from us, there was 1 more table occupied. Yet, our order took almost 20 minutes to come. May be they are preparing everything fresh hence the delay. The menu looked interesting and there were a few options for vegetarians. I got their free hummus through yelp check in, it was very tasty just like the soft and fluffy pita came along with it. I ordered a cauliflower dish and it was too greasy. My husband ordered the beef kebab platter and he liked it. Overall ok-ish experience.

The Emmy burger is fantastic but on the expensive side. They didn't ask what type of cook I wanted so make sure to specify if you want something other than medium / medium rare on the burger. I'll definitely be back to try the delicious looking pizzas.

Let me just say I came here for restaurant week and probably spent the same amount of money I would've spent outside of restaurant week but- It WAS TOTALLY WORTH IT!This restaurant and dining experience blew away all of my expectations for this place. I came here for my nieces graduation as I told her to pick out a place she would like to eat to celebrate her graduation. I was happy with the choice as I've always wanted to come here to eat as well. Upon walking in, we were greeted by really nice hostesses and staff. Since I made reservations we were seated right away in which we chose to sit outside. We came here for restaurant week and had a prix fix menu in which we all could order an entree each but we had to try something different; a communal style table setting in which we share dishes. Although I cannot remember the names, we had lettuce wraps, chicken on a stick and the drunken fish and the dishes were AMAZING (I can certainly remember the taste!)Everything from the service to the dishes to the atmosphere was top notch so I would definitely come back here!

I've had the pleasure of frequenting this fantastic lunch spot close to my workplace on several occasions. Their fish tacos and chicken schnitzel are particularly noteworthy and have become personal favorites. The staff here exudes warmth, ensuring that patrons feel like regulars in no time. While they offer a great bar setup, it's worth noting they serve beer and wine exclusively. A delightful dining experience that I highly recommend!

I literary ran here and was seated at the sushi bar before last call. It's beautiful and worth the extra steps!! Amazing sashimi!!I had hotate scallops Kimnedai Baby yellowtail Hamachi Scottish salmon Take was my sushi chef and he is featured in my Snapchat photo!This is the BOMB!! Trust me, Yelpers, I know my sashimi!By the way, the way I can tell how authentic a Japanese restaurant is has a lot to do with the music, ginger and fresh wasabi  A+

Strolling down St Marks we were looking for a nice place to grab a drink and a quick snack. Upon arrival, we were welcomed in by the host and shown to a table near their beautiful big front windows which are close to the street. As it was a cool spring night we were extremely pleased with the ambiance. All the brews on the menu (and there are a TON) are from local breweries. The Concrete Jungle Bird cocktail is very tasty and not too sweet. On the flip side, the Mango Margarita is fairly sweet...much sweeter then the Concrete Jungle Bird. Both were strong but were very tasty! I will definitely be back. This bar is very chill and perfect for a Saturday night.

I came here for a group gathering on a Thursday evening during happy hour. It definitely looks cool and the setup is organized - tons of long communal tables, enormous space (jeez, what's the rent here?!), dim lighting, sketches and paintings on the walls, extreme Oktoberfest vibes. But it's extremely crowded and loud that we were all pretty uncomfortable. The lines were so long both upstairs and downstairs that it deterred some from waiting for drinks or food. Also, the age range is under 26, so we, being between 29-25, were out-of-place. It's a great place for bros and for hanging out in groups. Don't come if you want to have conversations and kick back, because it's a rowdy place. Cool that they have trivia nights on Mondays!

We had a 10:30 pm reservation on July 4th. The place wasn't crowded at all. We waited an hour for our food in between our appetizers and our main meal. Steak frites was tough but well seasoned. Not worth it. The busboy was excellent, however. Very attentive.

- Standard diner vibes- They have window seating where you can people watch - I enjoyed the food- Many breakfast options that come with coffee/tea AND juice- Pancakes aren't so great- Service was good

My review is based off a Mealpal order.  I had gotten the pork katsu don order.  The pork was deliciously fried and went well with the egg over rice.  It came with a small side of pickled radish so that was a nice touch.  I did wish the portion was a tad bigger and that the order was warmer temperature wise.  I would give this place a strong 3 and will try their other options next time around.

Title: A Bustling Spot with Customizable Delights

I recently dined at a vibrant restaurant where the buzzing atmosphere is a clear testament to its popularity. The service proved to be impressively swift, and the offer of unlimited rice is a pleasant bonus. For my first foray into dried hot pot, the experience was both unique and customizable, allowing patrons to select their preferred ingredients and pay by weight.

The selection was diverse, including meats like beef and chicken, and an array of vegetables, with the lotus being a standout addition for me. Although the quail eggs weren't to my liking, the variety ensures there's something for everyone. The only shortfall was the lack of a DIY sauce station, which could have enhanced the meal with options such as peanut butter, sesame oil, and green onion to tailor the flavors to one's taste.

Nonetheless, the restaurant delivered an exciting culinary adventure that I'm eager to explore again. A return visit is certainly on the cards!

Super delicious burger! The beef is juicy with nice flavor.I had the regular cheeseburger with raw onion and the regular fixings that come with it. My friend had the jalapeño burger and loved it as well, claiming she had the best burger out of us. The milkshake was fresh and delicious. I got chocolate and banana, don't judge. It tastes like a sundae!

Title: Hit-and-Miss Experience at a New Dining Spot

I recently ventured to a new restaurant with my siblings, eager for a fresh culinary experience. The visit was a mixed bag, with the establishment showing promise yet leaving room for improvement.

Our server had an indifferent presence, often requiring reminders to supply extra napkins and clear plates. The array of dishes we sampled varied in satisfaction. The calamari, disappointingly reminiscent of onion rings, missed the mark. On the upside, the waffle fries were a delectable hit, and the crab cocktail claws emerged as the standout starter of the evening.

The main course of branzino fish was pleasing overall, although certain bites were regretfully oversalted. The combo of crab legs with shrimp, drenched in spicy special sauce, was decent but fell short of remarkable. It's tough to truly fault a seafood boil, though it wasn't the best I've had.

A generous gesture of a complimentary pound of crab legs and a bottle of soju capped off our meal. Despite the shortcomings, I hold out hope that the restaurant will refine its offerings, especially the appetizers, to reach its full potential.

Title: A Must-Visit for Italian Cuisine Lovers

Whenever I find myself in NYC, a visit to Mama Mia's is non-negotiable. The cuisine here consistently impresses with its rich flavors and generous portions, all at a price point that's a pleasant surprise for the city. On one occasion, I sampled their Marsala and found it to lean towards the sweet side, which was unexpected as I typically prefer a more savory take on the dish. Despite that personal preference, Mama Mia's remains a top recommendation for anyone in search of sumptuous Italian fare without the Manhattan price tag.

My friends took me here for my bachelorette brunch. I had such an amazing time. The food was delicious, mimosas were filled continuously, and the music was great. After we finished our meal we moved down to the dance floor which was down a level in like a "pit".  Our original plan was to leave and bar hop, but we continued to order champagne and bottle service to a table down in that area because the music and vibe was so good. If your looking for somewhere for a boozy brunch with great rap and hip hop music definitely give this place a try.

Recently, I was thrilled to accept a friend's invitation to a cozy little spot renowned for its boozy brunch. The compact size of the restaurant is easily overlooked once you dive into their culinary offerings. Our meal began with some off-menu guacamole, which proved to be a scrumptious precursor to the main event.

For my brunch entrée, I indulged in the ropa vieja served atop a plantain omelette. The flavors melded beautifully, and the portion size struck a harmonious balance—satisfying without being overbearing. My husband chose the Cuban sandwich, and his continuous compliments piqued my curiosity enough to steal a taste; it did not disappoint.

The brunch experience was sweetened by an hour and a half of unlimited drinks. While the beverages weren't standout, they were sufficiently enjoyable and contributed to a pleasant, buzzed state as we dined. All in all, this spot may be pint-sized, but it certainly packs a punch with its delightful fare.

Came here with my girlfriend for lunch. She wanted to come here because of the interior and she's been having somewhat of a British fever. The interior of this restaurant was really cute. The reason i give it 3 stars is i can see this place being great for a bar night to have a few drinks and chill, but for just lunch, it was average. I got a shepard pie and it was okay. My girlfriend got a burger and they didnt even ask how she wanted it cooked. In short, come for the interior and atmosphere, not for the food.

TLDR: Grab n' Go spot of Momofuku in Hudson Yards. If you're missing Asian convenience store food, worth stopping by. Spicy Chicken Kimbap.I had heard about Peach Mart opening in Hudson Yards so when I was finally in the area - I made a detour to check the place out. It is quite small and is sort of a simplified version of the corner stores you'll find in Asia.They have Asian soft drinks, snacks and some prepared foods too. The Stuffing Cake is basically a stuffing if you used ingredients for a college kid. Hot dogs, jalapenos, I liked this a lot actually. The rice and beans is good too.I do want to try some of the other sandwiches but the spicy chicken kimbap is solid. It's pricey at $11 but it's enjoyable. The chicken is still crispy although it's served at room temperature and also coated with the spicy mayo.There are seats/counters directly outside to sit. If you like Asian comfort food or ever wanted to try it, this is a good way to break yourself in.

I went in not exactly knowing what to expect for a Chinese restaurant in Hell's Kitchen, but I was pleasantly surprised with their expansive offerings! I was also surprised to see their tea offerings - something I've only seen available when I go to traditional dim sum places. The interior is pretty spacious, with plenty of seating available on a Saturday around 3pm on New Years Day. ROAST DUCK NOODLES - easily one of the best noodle dishes at this shop. The roast duck adds so much flavor to your broth it's insane!! I got the Chrysanthemum tea, and for my main dish, I went with the make your own noodle dish - chicken bone broth, ho fun (flat noodle), roast duck, and shanghai vegetables. Everything except the ho fun in this dish was on point! The ho fun was decent but could have been better - a lot of it was clumped together and broke off easily because of that. Portion sizes were great, however they could have added a few more pieces of duck to the dish. Otherwise, a great place to try some Chinese noodles if you're in the area.

My experience at Pardon My French left me with mixed emotions. Celebrating a birthday, the highlight was undoubtedly the spirited birthday song and a sparkler-adorned chocolate mousse that was sinfully delightful. Unfortunately, the rest of the meal did not live up to that moment.

The Eggs Scandinavian, while a solid attempt, fell short with an un-toasted English muffin undermining the dish's potential. Although I prefer my Hollandaise on the side, the overall combination was lackluster and did not justify its price, even when paired with the bottomless mimosas offered.

On a brighter note, the Brioche French Toast was a testament to indulgence. Thick, eggy slices of bread were lavished with Nutella and fresh fruit, which was a treat to the palate. Despite its quality, the $22 price tag before extra charges felt steep.

While the ambiance suggests Pardon My French is a trendy spot for a bottomless brunch, I find it hard to ignore the overpriced menu. I'm left doubtful about a return visit.

Title: A Cheesy Delight Before the Show

I stumbled upon a delightful grilled cheese spot while waiting for a movie in the area. Known for my love of their truffle melt, I was tempted by the new limited edition Notorious Chz melt - a decadent cheese extravaganza featuring six different cheeses and a hint of truffle mayo. This grilled melt was a cheese lover's dream, perfectly toasted and teeming with a symphony of flavors.

To complement the cheesy affair, we opted for the Chicken Tenders with a Buffalo Parmesan twist. They were exceptionally crispy with an intense spicy kick - a bit too fiery for my liking but satisfying for those who appreciate the heat.

The eatery itself is quaint with very limited seating, making it ideal for a swift grab-and-go experience. Prices align with similar establishments, and the service was commendably speedy. If you're in the mood for a top-notch grilled cheese, this place is a solid pick.

Got to know this restaurant through lunch takeouts! They do have the best miso salmon salads in town. It is definitely unbeatable with more than 10 different veggies and fruits and delicious miso salmon! However, the price is quite hefty for a salad ($26) so it is more of an indulgent experience than a daily order!

This is one of my favorite restaurants on the Upper West Side. Great for brunch or dinner and love that you can make reservations here unlike their other restaurant Jacobs Pickle. The honey pull apart bread is a true star. I could have eaten an entire order alone for my meal. If you are a fan of Reuben sammies, their Deluxe version is not to be missed. However, I prefer their Reuben hash at brunch! The classic Mac and cheese is great, but I prefer the buffalo version. While I love the chocolate cake it is ALOT and very dense. Will keep coming back!

Title: A Timeless Seafood Gem at Rockefeller Center

If you're seeking an exceptional seafood dining experience in NYC, this venerable spot in Rockefeller Center remains a top contender. A smart choice during Restaurant Week, it offers an affordable glimpse into an otherwise pricey menu. Our three-course delight started with a rich seafood bisque, a refreshing shrimp salad, and tantalizing crab cakes, setting a high bar for the courses to follow.

The main dishes - succulent salmon, delicate sole, perfect cod, and a finely crafted pasta - did not disappoint. Dessert rounded off the meal beautifully, complemented by a selection from their extensive wine list. The ambience added to our enjoyment, with a charming view of the ice-skating rink enhancing the restaurant's already enchanting atmosphere.

This place is a true classic that has stood the test of time, making it an ideal choice for those special occasions. Highly recommended for its enduring excellence in seafood dining.

Title: Airy Ambiance, Average Eats

I recently dined at a restaurant with a delightful dining room that was both airy and pleasant, creating a comfortable environment. For my meal, I chose the hanger steak, which unfortunately did not impress – it was rather average and lacked the wow factor that would tempt a second order. On a brighter note, the Sea Bass served at our table showed promise and was a more enjoyable choice. The saving grace of the experience was the staff, who were notably attentive throughout the meal. While the atmosphere was inviting, the food warrants some improvement to match the charm of the surroundings.

I came here for the big plate of chicken and it definitely did not disappoint! The place doesn't seat many people. Try to get here early or you'll be stuck waiting outside. BYOB if you wanna drink though! Also, the food is not that spicyThe cumin lamb and beef shumai were good but didn't blow me away. The sauteed crispy pancake actually comes with a choice of meat! I ended up ordering vegetarian but I think it would have been better with lamb or beef. The pancake itself was super crispy. Heavy cumin flavor though. Would not recommend if you do not like cumin. It was finally time for the star of the show - the big plate of chicken with bone!!! It comes with amazing noodles as its super soft and absorbs the flavor of the sauce. I could have just ate a bowl of noodles with that sauce. Chicken was also on point - very soft and flavorful. I would come back for the big plate of chicken!

Title: Authentic German Flavors with a Caution

If you're in the mood for a slice of Germany, this bar is a delightful spot offering a variety of authentic German drinks and decent bar fare, with their hamburger standing out as a crowd favorite. The ambiance is cozy and fitting for a German establishment. However, I'd advise exercising caution when navigating the stairs to the bathroom, especially after enjoying a couple of their excellent brews, as they can be unexpectedly treacherous. Overall, this place would have earned a full five stars, but due to the safety concern regarding the staircase, I have to dock one. Prost, but tread carefully!

My wife, brother, and I came here last night with colleagues. We had booked out the entire restaurant and it was because one of our colleagues said it was the best Taiwanese in New York. He is Canadian, so I was skeptical. It certainly did not disappoint.We tried everything on the menu, and the chef prepared off-menu items as well. The highlight was the beef noodle soup, which was flavorful and had an amazing broth. There are a number of customization options such as noodle texture, broth, type of meat, to fit anybody's expectations.The service was also spectacular; very attentive, and at the same time, very helpful as we had specific questions about the food in the restaurant.I cannot wait to come back here for breakfast, because it's an entirely different menu and it's supposed to be amazing as well. What a gem, and we will be back soon.

We made a brunch reservation for Valentine's day and it was surprisingly not every table was packed. I'd definitely go back, but for dinner I think it would be important to make a reservation. We had the truffle pasta and the carbonara, but I think the truffle pasta edged out the carbonara by a little bit on flavor and uniqueness.Truffle pasta: They was a decent amount of shaved truffle, but oddly not quite enough pasta. The dish was very rich and satisfying, but I easily could have eaten 2 of them.Carbonara: It needed a little more pancetta, but was otherwise rich and plated well with the egg yolk ready to be broken and mixed in with the rest of the pasta. I thought it was an excellent way to start the day!

I called beforehand on 24th asking the hours for HH that night. Arrived and seated and the waiter was like we don't have HH during the holidays. I said well I called earlier and that's not what whoever answered said. The waiter insisted. I then want to leave. And maybe a higher up guy told the waiter we can have it. Kind of a scam?? Well of course the rest of the mood was blown and waiter was with awkward attitude. Margherita Pizza was okay dough was watery. Mussel was pretty good.

I wanted ramen so I ventured out since I am using the mealapp (classic tonkotsu ramen).The place still had a closed sign showing even though I selected 12PM time period for the food pickup.  Most of the time the place has the food ready to go or need only a few minutes to get the food ready.  While at the restaurant, there are folks waiting for food to go in one section of the restaurant hanging out and there were some patrons seated reviewing their menu to order food. It tooked about 7-10 minutes before the food was ready.  All of a sudden, all the food items to go were ready at the same time and half the restaurant emptied out with our food bags.  Unfortunately I checked in and the time expired before I received my food.  It is considerate that they place the tonkotsu soup in a separate container than the dry ingredients.  Overall it is good though I could have used a bit more dry ingredients.Not bad though I think it's better to dine-in.

Great low key spot. They actually have something called the Vegan Platter and it's actually very good. I think they change up what's included but last time I was there it was two different eggplant spreads, hummus, surprisingly good beets, tabouleh and a basic little salad with whole wheat pita. All delicious. The time before that there was a chickpea salad instead of beets. It's a lot of food and will definitely fill you up and more, but it all feels healthy/light and guilt free. They definitely have wine, not sure about liquor. They will also split checks based on your actual dishes or however you want, which is nice.

Title: Cozy Dinner with Mixed Impressions

My visit to this bustling eatery on August 18th provided a quaint experience filled with swift service and fresh flavors. The bread set a promising start, arriving promptly to our table. The pizzas, served piping hot, were definitely the centerpiece of the meal. However, not all toppings hit the mark; the mushroom pie, laden with hefty chunks of fungi, might underwhelm those who aren't devout mushroom enthusiasts. On the flip side, the sausage pizza's flavors impressed, though its crust verged on excessively thin, even for a thin-crust aficionado like myself. Notably, the crust edges were delectably memorable.

Rounding off the meal, the tiramisu was a highlight, decadently creamy and perfect for sharing among our party of three. It's a generous portion that would be overwhelming for a solo diner. Overall, the experience was a palate-pleaser, despite some minor hitches in the pizza department.

Absolutely amazing! Very classy place, we went for a friends birthday and each of us got the pre fix brunch. They have multiple options from $30-$55, I got the $55 one with the special edition bottle of champagne, entree and juice are included as well. Service was attentive and food was delicious! My birthday is in a few weeks, I might be back!

Title: A Hidden Gem for Chinese Comfort Food

Following my brother's tip, I decided to check out this local hotspot reputed for its long lines and rave reviews. Much to my delight, the queue wasn't as daunting during my visit. The venue boasts an unbeatable combination of taste, value, and convenience, making it the go-to spot for a satisfying bite on a budget.

I opted for two small servings of roast pork over rice, which set me back a mere $8.50. This place punches well above its weight, delivering a meal that was both mouth-wateringly scrumptious and wallet-friendly. Each bite was a testament to the fact that great food doesn't have to be expensive.

This establishment has earned itself a repeat customer in me, especially for those days when the craving for quick and affordable Chinese eats strikes. A definite must-try!

I was extremely disappointed by the quality of the ramen here. It was also really overpriced. The classic tonkotsu was $18.90 and barely came with any toppings. Most of the toppings including the egg were extra to add to your ramen, which I thought was ridiculous for the price. Kae-dama (noodle refill) for $3.90 is also ridiculous. I've never seen a ramen restaurant charge that much for kaedama. I know noodles aren't that expensive. I understand that they're a no tipping restaurant but their prices just seem overly inflated. The noodles were way overcooked even though I ordered firm. They came out more like soft. I probably should have ordered extra firm, but you would think that a place like Ichiran would have perfected their timing on the noodles. The broth was average. It had flavor but lacked a wow factor. Overall I didn't have a good experience due to the quality and price . You're much much better off going to a number of ramen places in New York including Ippudo. I was so disappointed that this location is making all the Ichirans look bad. It's a much higher standard in Japan.

I've been itching to try KazuNori for so long and it definitely did not disappoint! It's a small restaurant that only serves hand rolls. Their seating is exclusively bar-style, which allows every diner to witness the sushi chefs make the rolls on demand. My friend and I chose to share the 6 roll set because we thought it would be a better deal than ordering each roll separately. The set had the Toro, Yellowtail, Salmon, Bay Scallop, Crab, and Lobster hand rolls. Of the bunch, I tried the Toro, Salmon, and Lobster. Each time, I was amazed at how fresh the fish were. The fish and seasoned rice paired together so perfectly that soy sauce or wasabi seemed superfluous.Turns out that 6 rolls was not filling enough for 2 people. I'm too accustomed to eating cone hand rolls stuffed with rice, but these definitely had a better rice to fish ratio. I ordered a Bay Scallop roll and decided it was my favorite. The scallop is slightly sweet, smooth, and buttery. KazuNori definitely tops my list of places for a quick, light lunch. Their fish is so fresh, it'll blow any competition out of the water.

Prince Street Pizza is probably my all time favorite pizza place! There is so much flavor to every bite of the pizza! The pepperoni is definitely a crowd favorite, so you must get a slice of that if it is your first time! The line is quite long during lunch and dinner hours, but in between, it is just a short 10-15 minute wait! (~3:45-4pm is a pretty solid time to go when the line is shorter)!

Title: A Flavorful Fusion with Room for Improvement

I recently dined at a restaurant that offers a tantalizing mix of Cajun and Asian cuisine, ideal for those who appreciate robustly seasoned dishes. The service was a high point, with Angus providing attentive care and excellent food recommendations.

On the culinary front, the blue crab in salted yolk stood out as a spectacular starter, both in flavor and portion, perfect for sharing. The King Crab, pre-cut and bathed in spicy Cajun sauce, was delightful, though the serving size did not quite justify the price. The crawfish, on the other hand, offered great value, boasting unbeatable freshness.

The atmosphere was pleasingly pristine, with the thoughtful addition of upstairs seating. The food menu was extensive, highlighted by the freshness of the seafood and a variety of combo options. Complimentary roasted peanuts, tea, and a small fruit plate bookended the meal charmingly.

However, the dining experience was not without its drawbacks. The provided gloves for seafood boils were disappointingly flimsy, a minor but notable detraction from the otherwise enjoyable experience. The beverage selection was limited, with wines only available by the bottle at a steep price, and the absence of a dessert menu (or offer) left a sweet gap in the meal.

Despite these areas for improvement, the overall experience was positive, and I anticipate a return visit to indulge once more in their delightful seafood offerings. The total bill for two was $140 plus tip, sizeable but not outlandish considering the quality and setting.

During a visit back in July, I had the pleasure of indulging in a Wimbledon breakfast at this charming little eatery. The highlight was a delightful mushroom omelette, accompanied by crisp hash browns and a side of spicy ketchup which added a nice kick to the meal. Whether you're popping in for a hearty breakfast, a leisurely lunch, or a cozy dinner, this quaint spot certainly doesn’t disappoint. Highly recommended for a satisfying dining experience!

Following a day at Comicon, a friend's recommendation led me to this no-frills pizza spot known for its efficiency more than its ambiance. True to form, it's a grab-and-go kind of place, not designed for leisurely dining, but perfectly suited for the bustling commuter crowd.

For a mere dollar a slice, expectations were easily met—neither dazzled nor disappointed. The pizza itself was a decent rendition of the classic New York style that's become a beloved staple. Standing at a counter, my group and I quickly devoured our slices before continuing on with our day.

In sum, it offered a satisfactory, if not memorable, experience. Personally, I prefer a more traditional sit-down meal, but for the on-the-go diner in search of an economical bite, this spot does the trick.

I recently grabbed lunch at this spot using a fantastic $1 deal via the Ritual app, opting for the pan-fried classic dumplings. The flavor was delightful, and the two accompanying sauces complemented the dumplings perfectly. However, the dumplings tended to fall apart at the seams with each bite, which made for a challenging eating experience. The dining area is quite compact, offering just a few counter seats. Despite the small space, the service was efficient, and my order was prepared right on schedule.
